# Results — Study 727 ("the Quebec strategic maple-syrup reserve as a trade")

*Generated by [`examples/verify.py`](../examples/verify.py). Can you trade maple syrup? We
test the strongest tradable version of "the maple reserve is a commodity trade": the
**administered PPAQ bulk price** (hardcoded, cited, **approximate** — a labelled proxy, not
a live feed; there is no maple exchange), the only **listed** way to touch maple (Rogers
Sugar `RSI.TO`, with a sugar-futures `SB=F` placebo), each benchmarked against the S&P/TSX
Composite (`^GSPTSE`), and a sugaring-season (Feb–Apr) seasonal. Offline & deterministic;
run `python examples/verify.py` to reproduce every number.*

## Data stamp

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| Maple price | **Hardcoded, cited, approximate** annual PPAQ bulk price of Grade A syrup (CAD/lb, 2008–2024), reconstructed from producers'-cartel reporting — see [`docs/references.md`](references.md). **A PROXY, not a feed** (fingerprint `123be1d12a41`). |
| Equity proxies | `RSI.TO` (Rogers Sugar, TSX — Lantic refiner + L.B. Maple Treat/Decacer maple unit) · `SB=F` (No.11 sugar futures — a *placebo*, not maple) — month-end Adj Close via yfinance, cached under `_cache/` |
| Benchmark | `^GSPTSE` (S&P/TSX Composite, month-end Adj Close — CAD, so no FX mismatch with RSI.TO) |
| As-of | 2026-06-01 (month-end; data runs to 2026-05) |
| Equity window | 2010-01 → 2026-05 (RSI.TO/TSX: 196 monthly returns; SB=F: 167) · fingerprint `2f0f50f97e59` |

> **Why proxies, stated as a decision.** There is **no maple-syrup exchange, no futures,
> no live price API** — the world price is *administered* by the Quebec producers' cartel
> (PPAQ) and defended by a strategic reserve. Rather than fabricate a live tape we (a)
> hardcode a small, clearly-cited, **approximate** annual series whose *shape* — a
> near-flat, committee-set creep — is the load-bearing fact, and (b) test the only
> **tradable** thing with real maple exposure, a listed sugar refiner. A refiner's equity
> is **not** the price of a barrel of syrup; it is a labelled proxy throughout.

## Half 1 — does holding maple pay? (administered price vs TSX)

The (approximate, cited) PPAQ bulk price, annual CAD/lb:

| year | 2008 | 2010 | 2012 | 2014 | 2016 | 2018 | 2020 | 2022 | 2023 | 2024 |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| CAD/lb | 2.60 | 2.72 | 2.92 | 2.90 | 2.85 | 2.85 | 2.85 | 3.02 | 3.35 | 3.60 |

The price is *set*, not discovered: it barely moves for a decade, then a modest 2022–24
inflation-era catch-up. Headline risk/return vs the TSX:

| series | CAGR | ann. vol | Sharpe | max drawdown |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| **PPAQ maple price** | **+2.05%** | **3.5%** | 0.61 | −3.4% |
| S&P/TSX (year-end) | **+4.45%** | 11.9% | — | −11.6% |

**Maple lost the race** — ~2%/yr vs the index's ~4.5%/yr — while being *engineered* not to
move (a real soft commodity swings 25–40%/yr). The mean annual excess (maple − TSX) is
**−3.0%/yr, t = −0.91** (p = 0.38, n = 14 years): no evidence maple rewards a holder better
than stocks, and the point estimate is negative. The low volatility is the *signature of an
administered price*, not a free lunch.

## Half 2 — the tradable proxies vs TSX (the only thing you can buy)

Monthly Adj Close, Newey-West (6-lag) alpha vs `^GSPTSE`. **These are labelled proxies.**

| series | CAGR | ann. vol | Sharpe | max DD | alpha/yr | beta | NW *t*(α) | p |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| **RSI.TO** (Rogers Sugar) | +9.39% | 15.7% | 0.65 | −24.4% | +6.56% | +0.50 | **+1.83** | 0.069 |
| **SB=F** (sugar futures, placebo) | −4.52% | 33.4% | 0.00 | **−69.4%** | +1.71% | −0.21 | +0.19 | 0.848 |
| ^GSPTSE | +7.25% | 11.9% | 0.65 | −22.7% | — | — | — | — |

Rogers Sugar out-returned the index, but its alpha **does not clear the |t| ≥ 2 bar**
(*t* = 1.83) — `WEAK` at most — and it is the *wrong kind* of edge: a **low-beta (0.50),
dividend-paying refiner** earns a classic defensive premium that has nothing to do with the
(flat) maple bulk price. Attributing it to maple is a **misattribution**. The genuinely
tradable sweetener, sugar futures, lost ~4.5%/yr with a −69% drawdown — the nearest soft
commodity to maple, and a disaster. **No harvestable, maple-attributable alpha in either.**

## Half 3 — the sugaring-season seasonal (Feb–Apr) on RSI.TO

Per-calendar-month one-sample HAC *t* of RSI.TO monthly returns (the multiple-comparisons
trap made explicit — test 12 months and one lights up by chance):

| month | Jan | **Feb** | **Mar** | **Apr** | May | Jun | Jul | Aug | Sep | Oct | Nov | Dec |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| mean % | −0.0 | +1.5 | +1.8 | +0.6 | +0.2 | +0.9 | **+2.2** | −0.5 | +1.2 | −1.5 | +2.5 | +1.5 |
| HAC *t* | −0.0 | +1.8 | +2.6 | +1.0 | +0.2 | +1.6 | **+5.1** | −0.5 | +1.9 | −1.6 | +2.0 | +2.1 |

The sugaring months (Feb–Apr, **bold**) do not stand out; the single loudest month is
**July** (HAC *t* = 5.1) — which has **no** sugaring story, the multiple-comparisons trap in
one column. Pooled, Feb–Apr vs the rest:

| | value |
|---|--:|
| Feb–Apr mean | +1.28%/mo (n = 51) |
| rest-of-year mean | +0.70%/mo (n = 145) |
| **spread** | **+0.58%/mo**, Welch **t = 0.81** |
| block-bootstrap 95% CI on spread | **[−0.71%, +1.95%]** — spans 0 |

**No tradable sugaring seasonal.** A long-in-spring / hold-the-index-otherwise timer
(one-way 15 bp/leg × NAV, Sharpe excess-of-benchmark both legs):

| strategy | CAGR | Sharpe (exc-TSX) |
|---|--:|--:|
| sugaring timer (gross) | +9.11% | 0.22 |
| sugaring timer (net 15 bp/leg) | +8.78% | 0.18 |
| **buy & hold RSI.TO** | **+9.38%** | 0.16 |
| buy & hold TSX | +7.24% | — |

Timing the "season" **loses to simply holding the stock** (net 8.78% < 9.38%): it steps out
of good non-spring months and pays spreads to do it.

## Synthetic positive control — the seasonality engine is faithful

A deterministic monthly world with a *planted* +6%/yr Feb–Apr premium (seed 727): the
engine recovers the up-sign with **spread +3.30%/mo, t = +3.77, `sign_ok = 1`**. The
harness can bank a planted season, so the flat sugaring result on the real tape is a **real
null**, not a broken pipeline.

## Verdict

- **Signal — NONE.** The administered maple price grew ~2%/yr (below stocks, near-flat by
  design; annual excess **−3.0%/yr, t = −0.91**); the only buyable proxy's alpha is
  **t = 1.83 < 2** and is defensive-sugar beta, not maple; the sugaring-season spread is
  **t = 0.81** with a CI through 0. No robust *t* ≥ 2 tied to maple anywhere.
- **Tradability — MIRAGE.** There is **no maple market** — no exchange, no futures, a
  committee-set price. The only buyable expression is a defensive sugar refiner
  (β = 0.50); the sugaring-season timer nets **8.78%/yr, below buy-&-hold RSI.TO (9.38%)**.
  Capacity is fatal: there is no instrument to size into.
- **Just a curio? — CONFIRMED.** A superb story — cartel, ~100 M-lb strategic reserve, a
  ~C$18.7 M heist — with no tradable edge attached. The reserve exists to *remove* the
  volatility a trader would need.

> **Caveat (named, not buried).** The maple price here is a **small, hardcoded, approximate**
> reconstruction of the negotiated PPAQ bulk price — its near-flat *shape* is defensible but
> its precise year values are not a live feed, and the annual *t* rests on 14 observations.
> The equity proxies are exactly that — proxies for "touching the maple trade," not the price
> of a barrel. Both limitations push the verdict toward humility, not toward a stronger claim:
> nothing here says maple is tradable, and several lines say the opposite.
